value.title: Location cursor stays above every map object
value.statement: Treat user-location-layer as a render-only overlay outside LayerGroup order, with the compass-uncertainty sector and metric accuracy fill immediately below it; restore that five-layer stack (accuracy, heading fill, white heading halo, blue heading outline, symbol) above user layers after cold, lite and hot mutations and clear an expired GPS indicator only if no retained network display estimate remains. Retained network estimates keep original timestamp/accuracy and show their age; they never become fresh recording fixes. The centered Orbit ring keeps a transparent 21 dp opening around a 5 dp blue dot with a 2 dp white border; its blue rim grows outward to radius 13 dp inside the unchanged 15.2 dp white outer rim and dark edge. Accuracy and compass geometry leave the opening clear so smaller user points below the cursor remain visible without tinting or changing layer order. The ring does not move when its outlined triangle rotates. Valid true compass heading wins even at rest; missing, unavailable, unreliable or stale compass hides its sector and immediately falls back to a moving fix's valid course, or hides the triangle when neither direction is available. Default all three compass-sector layers to hidden; honor the saved show_compass_accuracy_sector checkbox on map resume and across cold/hot/lite reload via MapDrawable.setCompassAccuracySectorVisible. Preserve geometry, styling and uncertainty calculations for future calibration without disabling the direction arrow or GPS accuracy. Keep the retained sector length 56 logical map pixels across zoom and its angle independent of metric GPS accuracy; actively expire compass readings after 500 ms without a GPS callback. Only the phone GPS status number and circle use a 3 m display floor; preserve external input, native NMEA, mock GPS, Network and every provider Location used for filtering and recording.
